question: A train covers the distance between two stations X and Y in 6 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 13 km/h, then it travels the same distance in 9 hours. Find the distance between the two stations
solution:
**Given:**

A train covers the distance between two stations X and Y in 6 hours. If the speed of the train is reduced by 13 km/h, then it travels the same distance in 9 hours.

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the station X and Y be d and the initial speed of the train be v

Then, d = 6v

When the speed of the train is reduced by 13km/h, the equation can be written as d = 9(v-13).

Substituting v=(d)/(6) in the above equation and solving for d,

d=9( (d)/(6) -13)

d=(3d)/(2) -117

d = 234km

**∴ The distance between the two stations is 234 km.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Let the initial speed be x

Distance = Speed × Time 

According to the question,

⇒ x × 6 = (x - 13) × 9

⇒ 6x = 9x - 117

⇒ 3x = 117

⇒ x = 39 kmph

Distance = 39 × 6 = 234 km. 

∴ The distance between the two stations is 234 km.
